sources.title: WH_KEYBOARD_LL doesn't work on Administrator mode applications
User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) Affects Hooks

findings.claim: Windows User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) blocks low-level keyboard hooks from capturing inputs generated inside elevated (Administrator) windows when the hook process itself runs as a standard user.
evidence: Win32 security boundaries prevent lower-integrity processes from intercepting messages sent to higher-integrity processes.
Running the target game (or its launcher, Steam) as administrator while running EasySpecy as standard user results in zero keyboard events captured.
sources: WH_KEYBOARD_LL doesn't work on Administrator mode applications

findings.claim: Games using DirectInput, XInput, or Raw Input bypass the standard Windows message queue entirely for keyboard input, preventing WH_KEYBOARD_LL from intercepting keypresses.
evidence: DirectInput/Raw Input queries input state directly from drivers, bypassing standard WM_KEYDOWN message pumps.

findings.claim: Kernel-level anti-cheat software (like Easy Anti-Cheat or BattlEye) blocks global user-mode hooks (SetWindowsHookEx) as a countermeasure against macros and key injection.
evidence: Hook callbacks are stripped or blocked system-wide when a protected game window has active focus.
sources: WH_KEYBOARD_LL doesn't work on Administrator mode applications

recommendation: Run the EasySpecy recorder with Administrator privileges to match integrity levels, or register for Raw Input (RegisterRawInputDevices) in the Rust backend instead of using standard Win32 hooks.
